import re
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def add_days(text, n):
    # Regular expression pattern to match the date format YYYY-MM-DD
    date_pattern = r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$'
    
    # Check if the input text matches the date pattern
    if not re.match(date_pattern, text):
        raise ValueError('Invalid date format')
    
    # Split the input text by hyphens to extract the year, month, and day as strings
    year, month, day = map(int, text.split('-'))
    
    # Create a datetime object from the year, month, and day
    date_obj = datetime(year, month, day)
    
    # Add or subtract n days from the datetime object
    new_date_obj = date_obj + timedelta(days=n)
    
    # Check if the resulting date is within the valid range of years from 1 to 9999
    if new_date_obj.year < 1 or new_date_obj.year > 9999:
        raise ValueError('Resulting date is outside the valid range of years from 1 to 9999')
    
    # Convert the resulting datetime object back to the YYYY-MM-DD format and return it
    return new_date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
